title: Merge alternatives for customer‑facing integrations in 2026
summary: Compare Merge alternatives by category: Kombo, Finch, and Bindbee for HRIS and ATS; Codat, Rutter, and Chift for accounting; Apideck, Unified.to, and Nango for CRM and file storage.
body_markdown:
The best Merge (merge.dev) alternative depends on which integration category your product needs most:


- **HRIS, ATS, and payroll:** Kombo, or Finch if you only need US payroll and benefits data. Bindbee fits early-stage teams with straightforward HRIS read needs or a focus on the Indian market.
- **Accounting, banking, and commerce:** Codat, Rutter, or Chift.
- **CRM, ticketing, and file storage:** Apideck, Unified.to, or Nango.

## **Respect where it’s due**


Merge is a great product, built by a capable team. Its Unified API and Agent Handler combine broad integration category coverage with enterprise readiness and mature developer tooling. And with their recent product expansions of Gateway and Merge for Workforce, it now also covers governing employees’ internal AI use.


This makes Merge a strong fit if you’re looking for:


- **Broad coverage across categories and systems from one vendor:** Merge’s Unified API covers eight categories (HRIS, ATS, CRM, accounting, ticketing, file storage, knowledge base, and chat) with 200+ integrations listed in its docs, and Agent Handler adds hundreds of MCP-ready connectors that let AI agents take actions in third-party tools. If your product needs some HR data alongside CRM, accounting, or ticketing data, Merge is a strong choice.
- **Governing your own employees’ AI use:** Merge for Workforce pushes approved models, MCP servers, and skills to employees’ AI tools via Okta, Entra, or another identity provider, with cost controls and audit logging.


But this breadth comes with a trade-off. If you’re primarily looking for one or two integration categories from one vendor, you should consider vertical specialists as an alternative.


## **How to choose a vertical Merge alternative**


Technical product and engineering leaders tend to evaluate a vertical Merge alternative on six dimensions:


1. **Category focus:** What share of your integration usage sits in one category today, and where will it sit in 24 months?
2. **Write coverage on your customers’ systems:** Connector counts matter, but they don’t tell you whether an integration supports your use case in production. Ask for the list of systems where the exact operation you need works today, such as creating employees in HRIS, updating application stages in ATS, or creating invoices in accounting.
3. **Data model depth:** What unified data models are covered per category and for how many integrations they are actually built out.
4. **Roadmap focus:** What share of next year’s engineering roadmap goes into your category? A vendor that adds new product lines can still be a good vendor, but your category gets a smaller share of its engineers’ time.
5. **Support on enterprise systems:** Who fixes it when a sync breaks? The first sync of a large Workday or SAP SuccessFactors tenant often runs into rate limits and timeouts, so find out whether your plan gets you the engineers who built the integration or a ticket queue.
6. **Implementation track record:** How many customer tenants has the vendor connected on the systems you need? Customized systems like Workday and SAP SuccessFactors surface new edge cases with almost every tenant, so a vendor that has only seen a handful will still be fixing them on yours. Merge, for example, labels 59 of its 143 HRIS and ATS integrations as[beta](https://help.merge.dev/articles/5735015-beta-integrations) , meaning they lack widespread customer adoption.


Vendor facts in the sections below come from each vendor’s own website, docs, and blog, checked on October 19, 2026.


## **Merge alternatives for HRIS, ATS, and payroll integrations**


For HRIS, ATS, payroll, LMS, and assessment integrations, the vertical alternative to Merge is Kombo. Finch is a narrower option for teams that only need US payroll and benefits data. Bindbee fits early-stage teams with straightforward HRIS read needs or a focus on the Indian market. For broader comparisons within one category, see the best unified APIs for[HRIS integrations](https://www.kombo.dev/blog/best-unified-api-hris-integrations) and[ATS integrations](https://www.kombo.dev/blog/best-unified-api-ats-integrations) .


### Kombo


**What it is:** Kombo is a unified API built exclusively for HR and people data. As of October 2026, it supports 85 API-based HRIS integrations, including payroll systems such as ADP Workforce Now, Paychex, Gusto, and DATEV. It also supports 108 ATS integrations, 18 assessment and background-check integrations, and 10 LMS platforms such as Workday Learning, SAP SuccessFactors Learning, Cornerstone OnDemand, and Docebo.


**Data model and write depth:** Kombo has 18 common data models in HRIS and 20 in ATS, including[skills](https://docs.kombo.dev/hris/v1/get-skills) ,[performance](https://docs.kombo.dev/hris/features/performance-data) , and[staffing entities](https://docs.kombo.dev/hris/features/staffing-entities) . It also supports write operations such as[creating employee records](https://docs.kombo.dev/hris/implementation-guide/create-employee) in HRIS or[moving applications to a new stage](https://docs.kombo.dev/ats/v1/put-applications-application-id-stage) in ATS.


**Sync architecture:** Kombo is webhook-first. Where the underlying system sends webhooks, Kombo forwards data changes to you in real time, and a scheduled sync runs underneath to catch missed events and deletions. That sync runs every three hours by default and down to every five minutes on higher plans.


**Support level:** Every plan includes a shared Slack or Microsoft Teams channel with the engineers who built the integrations, based in New York City and Berlin. Kombo holds partnerships with Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle, and UKG. Customers choose an isolated US, Canada, or EU data center.


**Pricing:** An annual platform fee plus a per-customer fee for each connected end customer. Kombo doesn’t charge per API call ([pricing](https://www.kombo.dev/pricing) ).


**Best for:** B2B SaaS products whose integrations sit mostly in HR and recruiting, for example AI recruiting tools that write back to the ATS, assessment and background-check vendors, and HR or benefits platforms selling to enterprises on Workday or SAP SuccessFactors.


**Honest limitations:**


- No CRM, accounting, ticketing, file storage, or chat APIs. If you need those, you’re better served with Merge.
- Kombo offers SDKs in three languages, while Merge offers six.
- Prices aren’t published. Kombo quotes based on the number of connected customers and the features you need, after a free proof of concept ([pricing](https://www.kombo.dev/pricing) ).


**How it differs from Merge in HR and recruiting:** The gap is mostly in data model depth and write coverage. Kombo has 18 common HRIS models and 20 ATS models, compared to Merge’s 15 and 17, including skills, performance, and staffing entities, which Merge doesn’t offer. It creates employee records on 36 HRIS integrations, an operation Merge doesn’t support, and covers three to six times as many systems for ATS write operations.


### Finch


**What it is:**[Finch](https://www.tryfinch.com/) is a unified employment API for payroll, HR, and benefits data, listing 260 HRIS and payroll systems, of which 38 are API-based, and 100k+ connected employers. Its payroll model goes deep: pay statements break down into earnings, taxes, deductions, and contributions, and Finch writes employer contributions and employee deductions back into payroll, including 401(k) and Section 125 plans. It also syncs benefit enrollments and connects payroll with retirement recordkeepers.


Finch also reaches payroll systems that have no API. With[assisted integrations](https://developer.tryfinch.com/integrations/integration-types) , Finch’s team syncs the data as a third-party administrator in the employer’s system, which covers the other 222 systems for reads. Finch reports SOC 2 Type II compliance.


**Best for:** US benefits, 401(k), insurance, and fintech products that need line-item payroll data and deduction write-back, including for employers on payroll systems without an API.


**Honest limitations:**


- The HR data model is narrow. Finch’s products cover organization, payroll, deductions, and documents, with no unified models for time off, attendance, performance, or skills, and no core HR writes such as creating an employee.
- There’s no field mapping layer. Automated integrations return custom fields as raw data that you map in your own code, and assisted integrations don’t support custom fields at all.


**How it differs from Merge:** Finch is organized around payroll and benefits workflows like deductions, contributions, and recordkeeper sync, rather than a broad HR data model.


### Bindbee


**What it is:** Bindbee is a unified API for HRIS, payroll, and ATS data. It lists 54 HRIS systems, of which 50 are API-based, alongside 12 ATS integrations. It has strong coverage of Indian HR systems such as Darwinbox, Keka, and PeopleStrong, and offers on-premise and multi-geography hosting. Bindbee reports SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliance.


**Best for:** Early-stage teams with straightforward HRIS read needs, or products focused on the Indian market.


**Honest limitations:**


- The data model is mostly read-oriented. Bindbee covers 16 HRIS objects and documents writes for employees, payslips, timesheets, and time off, but doesn’t specify which systems support them. Skills and performance are listed in its docs, but no integration supports them.
- Bindbee has no enterprise HCM partnerships and no public track record with Workday or SAP SuccessFactors deployments.
- Custom field mapping has no transform layer, and syncs run every 24 hours by default.


**How it differs from Merge:** Bindbee covers fewer HRIS integrations than Merge, but adds strong Indian market coverage and on-premise hosting, which Merge doesn’t offer. See[Kombo vs. Bindbee](https://www.kombo.dev/blog/kombo-vs-bindbee) for a detailed comparison.


## **Merge alternatives for accounting, banking, and commerce**


Codat, Rutter, and Chift all specialize in financial data, and each has a clear home: Codat in lending and banking, Rutter in fintech products that combine accounting and commerce data, and Chift in European financial software.


### Codat


**What it is:**[Codat](https://www.codat.io/) connects to accounting, banking, and commerce platforms through standardized, two-way integrations. Business lenders, fintechs, and payment platforms use Codat Connect for underwriting, bill pay, expense management, and bank feeds, and Codat Insights turns the same accounting and ERP data into spend and working-capital insights for commercial banks.


**Best for:** Lenders, banks, and fintechs that need accounting and banking data for underwriting, portfolio monitoring, bank feeds, bill pay, or expense management.


**Honest limitations:** Codat is built for financial services. If you’re a SaaS company outside fintech, check that its standardized models cover your use case.


**How it differs from Merge:** Codat covers banking and commerce data, neither of which is one of Merge’s eight Unified API categories, and connects to on-premises accounting software.


### Rutter


**What it is:**[Rutter](https://www.rutter.com/) is a unified API for B2B financial products, with 75+ supported systems across accounting, ERP, commerce, and payments. It reads, updates, writes, and deletes data, sends webhooks for data changes, and lets you white-label the authentication flow your customers see.


**Best for:** Fintechs and banks building supplier enablement, invoicing automation, expense management, underwriting, or bank feeds, especially where accounting and commerce data meet.


**Honest limitations:** Rutter is built for financial and commerce data, so HR, CRM, or ticketing integrations need a second vendor.


**How it differs from Merge:** Rutter covers commerce and payments platforms. Merge’s Unified API has no category for either.


### Chift


**What it is:**[Chift](https://www.chift.eu/) is a unified API for European financial software. It lists 150+ connectors across six categories: accounting, point of sale, e-commerce, payments, invoicing, and property management systems (PMS). That includes the local and on-premises accounting software European SMBs run, such as ACD, Cegid, and Sage.


**Best for:** Products selling to European SMBs, where each country has its own accounting and invoicing software.


**Honest limitations:** Chift is built for the European market. If most of your customers are in North America, compare its connector list with the systems they use.


**How it differs from Merge:** Chift covers point of sale, invoicing, and PMS, which Merge’s eight categories don’t include, along with European accounting tools.[This blog post](https://www.chift.eu/blog/best-unified-api-platforms) from Chift goes deeper on the leading alternatives to Merge for accounting coverage.


## **Merge alternatives for CRM, ticketing, and file storage**


We didn’t find a vendor that specializes in CRM, ticketing, or file storage the way Kombo does in people data or Codat does in financial data. Your options are horizontal unified APIs and code-first platforms.


### Apideck


**What it is:**[Apideck](https://www.apideck.com/) now leads with accounting (50+ accounting and ERP systems). It also lists 22 CRM, 9 issue-tracking, and 5 file-storage integrations. Apideck doesn’t store customer data: every call is passed through to the source in real time. Billing is usage-based. Apideck is the closest to Merge’s multi-category model for teams that need CRM plus accounting and want zero data retention.


**Best for:** Teams that need CRM plus accounting from one vendor and want zero data retention.


**Honest limitations:** With no stored data, there’s no change detection, no historical state, and no replay of what a system looked like last week. Pricing has historically been per API call, which ties your bill to your read patterns.


### Unified.to


**What it is:**[Unified.to](https://unified.to/) lists 1,530+ integrations across 37 categories. Every request is a real-time passthrough call, and Unified.to doesn’t store end-customer data. Traffic runs in US, EU, or AU regions, and pricing scales with API volume rather than with the number of customers. It’s a fit if you need many categories at once and prefer passthrough over sync.


**Best for:** Teams that need many integration categories at once and prefer pass-through over sync.


**Honest limitations:** Depth per category is thin relative to the category count. In a pass-through model, upstream rate limits and outages surface directly in your product, and there’s no built-in sandbox.


### Nango


**What it is:**[Nango](https://www.nango.dev/) is a code-first platform. You write integration logic as code, with auth, syncs, and webhooks handled for you. Nango supports 1,000+ APIs with 7,000+ templates, is open source and can be self-hosted. Unlike Merge, there’s no fixed common model. You get more control, but have to maintain the integration code yourself.


**Best for:** Teams whose integrations are a core part of their product and who have the engineering bandwidth to build on top of Nango.


**Honest limitations:** You need to understand each underlying API and maintain every model and mapping yourself. Edge cases in systems like Workday and SAP SuccessFactors surface over months of production traffic, not during the first build.

## **When Merge is still the right choice**


Merge is the better fit in these cases:


- **You need HR data and CRM, accounting, or ticketing data from one API.** Merge’s Unified API covers eight categories with 200+ integrations listed in its docs. A single contract and data model across those categories is worth more than vertical depth if your product needs them all.
- **You need APAC hosting or a single-tenant deployment.** Merge offers US, EU, and APAC multi-tenant hosting plus single-tenant. Kombo offers US, Canada, and EU multi-tenant.


## **Frequently asked questions**


What are the best Merge.dev alternatives in 2026?


+


The best Merge alternative depends on which integration category you use most. For HRIS, ATS, payroll, LMS, and assessment integrations, Kombo is the vertical alternative, with 193 API-based HRIS and ATS integrations as of October 2026. Finch fits teams that only need US payroll and benefits data, and Bindbee fits early-stage teams with straightforward HRIS read needs or a focus on the Indian market. For accounting, banking, and commerce, look at Codat, Rutter, or Chift. For CRM, ticketing, and file storage, horizontal options like Apideck and Unified.to, or code-first Nango, are the closest fits.


What is the best Merge alternative for HRIS and ATS integrations?


+


Kombo is the unified API built only for people data. As of October 2026, it supports 85 API-based HRIS integrations and 108 ATS integrations, compared with Merge’s 80 and 63. Kombo supports more write operations, such as posting applications on 103 ATS integrations (Merge: 24), moving applications to a new stage on 52 (Merge: 17), and posting screening-question answers on 56 (Merge: 9). Kombo also creates employee records on 36 HRIS integrations, which Merge doesn’t support.


Does Merge support creating employees in an HRIS?


+


No. Merge’s HRIS write coverage is limited to time-off requests and timesheet entries. Kombo creates employee records on 36 HRIS integrations.


Is Kombo a Merge alternative?


+


Yes. Kombo is a unified API for HRIS, ATS, payroll, LMS, and assessment integrations, so it replaces Merge’s HRIS and ATS categories. It doesn’t offer CRM, accounting, ticketing, file storage, or chat, so teams that use those Merge categories would need another vendor for them.


When is Merge the better choice?


+


When you need HR data and CRM, accounting, or ticketing data from one API, or when you need APAC hosting or a single-tenant deployment.


Is Kombo only for European companies?


+


No. Kombo hosts customer data in the US, Canada, or the EU, and customers choose the region during onboarding. Kombo has teams in New York City and Berlin and is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. Kombo holds certified partnerships with Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle, and UKG.


How hard is it to migrate from Merge to Kombo?


+


Migrating from Merge to Kombo means swapping one unified API for another, so the integration model will be familiar to your team. Teams map their Merge common models to Kombo’s models, test every data flow in a Kombo sandbox, and get help from Kombo’s engineers during onboarding. One of Merge's featured case-study customers is currently migrating 300+ integrations to Kombo.


Does Kombo cover payroll and LMS?


+


Yes. Payroll systems such as ADP Workforce Now, Paychex, Paylocity, Gusto, PayFit, and DATEV connect through Kombo’s HRIS API. On Workday, UKG Pro, UKG Ready, and Dayforce, Kombo also returns payslips with line items and pay runs. Kombo’s LMS API covers 10 learning platforms as of October 2026, including Workday Learning, SAP SuccessFactors Learning, Cornerstone OnDemand, Docebo, and LinkedIn Learning. Payroll and LMS data use the same authentication, webhooks, and support model as Kombo’s HRIS and ATS integrations.


Why isn’t StackOne in this comparison?


+


StackOne has deprecated its unified API in its documentation, so it’s no longer a like-for-like alternative to Merge’s Unified API.
